articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters' (Digest No.16)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: The Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) builds, owns and operates the transmitting equipment used to carry the programmes of the Independent Television and the Independent Local Radio Companies. The television programmes are brought to over 99% of the population by two UHF transmitter networks. The IBA has a vast experience in the procurement, operation and maintenance of UHF solid state transmitting equipment but only with output powers of up to, and including, 200 W. The author describes the experience and advantages gained to date by the use of solid state transmitters and transposers and explains, why solid state, in the foreseeable future, could play a major role in the realisation of systems with output powers of up to 20 kW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design philosophy for solid state transmitters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: Many aspects of the complete transmitter design such as the number and size of RF modules, the number of power supplies, the cooling arrangement, method of combining modules, drive arrangement and, in the case of television, the method of combining sound and vision signals, all require consideration. A transmitter which meets all these requirements can be used without the need for a complete reserve transmitter and is said to possess 'Integral Modular Reserve'. The paper discusses these requirements and describes a design of a solid state FM broadcast transmitter which is based on this philosophy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technologies for all solid state TV transmitter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: Toshiba developed an all solid state 50 kW VHF TV transmitter and an all solid state 30 kW UHF TV transmitter in 1985. The technologies embodied in these solid state transmitters are described. The 50 kW visual power amplifier block consists of forty 1.5 kW visual power amplifiers, and the 12.5 kW aural power amplifier block is composed of ten 1.5 kW aural power amplifiers. These power amplifiers consist of power MOS field effect transistors (FETs) 2SK410s. The 30 kW power amplifier block consists of thirty-six 1.0 kW visual power amplifiers, and the 7.5 kW aural power amplifier block is composed of twelve 800 W power amplifiers. These power amplifiers consist of 2SC3702s bipolar transistors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New developments in transistorised TV transmitters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: Deals with new developments in solid state TV transmitters and describes some of the author's current work in this field. The range of high power solid state VHF and UHF TV transmitters developed by THOMSON-LGT uses a common set of techniques, including amplifiers power combining systems, DC power supply and distribution systems. The common set of techniques are illustrated by reference to the 30 kW VHF transmitter, as an example. The availability of VHF transistors with individual power ratings of 240 watts now allows the design of a television transmitter of 30 kW peak visual output power with high reliability, broadband operation, no tuning, excellent performance, and minimum maintenance requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A newly designed UHF solid-state television transmitter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: This brand new television transmitter (TV TX) is a fully transistorized TV transmitter using a 6 kW UHF transistor power amplifier (V6KDU TR PA) composed of eight 800 W transistor power amplifier modules and allows all solid-state UHF TV transmitters with high output powers to be achieved. This TV transmitter achieves a high reliability and maintainability by using a complete plug-in type connection between the transistor power amplifier (TR PA) modules (V800 DU TR PA), power supply modules (180A28VPS) and combiner. The elimination of the conventional heat sink from the TR PA modules leads to a light weight and high cooling efficiency by a newly developed system called 'jet air cooling'. This paper describes the outline and reliability of this recently developed TV transmitter, in particular, UHF 30 kW TV transmitter, consisting of 2 sets of complete 15 kW transmitters in parallel operation with exciter changeover facilities, while explaining new technologies applied in this TV transmitter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modular approach to solid state AM broadcast transmitters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: The gradual movement from transmitters employing thermionic valves to transmitters using transistors has almost always been accompanied by the use of a 'modular' form of construction. For powers exceeding 100 Watts or so a multiplicity of devices is required. There are technical problems in merely connecting the devices in parallel or series, so the resultant circuitry obviously divides into a number of blocks and can be constructed as such. However, there are decisions to be made concerning just what constitutes a 'module'. This paper addresses some of these questions without necessarily giving definite answer but giving examples of solutions. The type of transmitters the author has been concerned with have been relatively low power medium frequency amplitude modulated transmitters. The examples, therefore, concern mainly this type of transmitter, but may have relevance to other power levels and frequency bands.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TV linear power transistors for Band I, II, III, IV and V
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: Presents the parameters of the following transistors: the SD 1476 for Bands I and II (55-88 MHz) with a power output P/sub OUT/ of 240 W; SD 1483 for FM (88-108 MHz) with P/sub OUT/=250 W; SD 1485 for Band III (170-230 MHz) with P/sub OUT/=200 W; and SD 1492 for Bands IV and V (470-860 MHz) with P/sub OUT/=150 W. The advances in the transistors and the die characterisation data that was required to optimise the device parameters for best application performance are also covered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative ownership costs of UHF TV transmitters 5-15 kW peak sync
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advances in Solid State Technology for Broadcast Transmitters
abstract: For some years now there has been considerable interest in comparing the true ownership costs of tetrode and klystron UHF TV transmitters. This interest recently intensified with the advent of the all-solid-state transmitters up to the 40 kW peak sync level (PS). The author has attempted to arrive at the comparative ownership costs of the three types of transmitter and to show which is the most economically advantageous to the operator at the 5, 10 and 15 kW peak sync levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
